name: Renal Tubular Acidosis Type 2 (Proximal RTA)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proximal Renal Tubular Acidosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of impaired bicarbonate reabsorption in proximal tubules with increased urinary bicarbonate loss
Presence of normal anion gap (hyperchloremic) metabolic acidosis
Urine pH <5.5 after systemic acidemia is corrected
Presence of hypokalemia due to renal potassium wasting
Exclusion of distal (Type 1) renal tubular acidosis features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired bicarbonate reabsorption with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and urine pH <5.5 after correction of acidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of other causes of metabolic acidosis and may involve bicarbonate loading tests.

searchTerms: acid-base imbalance with normal anion gap
metabolic acidosis without increased anion gap

occasional.notes: Due to chronic acidosis and phosphate wasting
Due to proximal tubular phosphate wasting

rare.notes: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction including aminoaciduria and glycosuria
Kidney stone formation secondary to altered tubular handling
Occasionally observed due to tubular losses

laboratory: Glycosuria and aminoaciduria in Fanconi syndrome
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
Bone X-rays showing rickets or osteomalacia
genetic: Mutations in SLC4A4 gene (NBCe1 transporter) in inherited forms
other: Bicarbonate loading test demonstrating proximal tubular bicarbonate leak

distinguishingFeatures: Distal tubular defect with inability to acidify urine (urine pH >5.5)
Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction including glycosuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia
Often secondary to toxins, drugs, or inherited metabolic disorders
More widespread tubular defects beyond bicarbonate reabsorption

references: Karet FE. Inherited distal renal tubular acidosis. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2001;12(8):1548-1557.
Batlle DC, Haque SK. Genetic causes and mechanisms of distal renal tubular acidosis. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2012;27(10):3691-3704.
